assumptions.salt_scope: per session, not per (arm, policy, session) as in U4: a per-arm salt would make the pre-fork prompts differ and force 264 requests. Cold isolation across sessions is preserved; the two arms share only the pre-fork bytes, which are identical by construction.

evidence.answer_G1: fork and summarise-in-place do NOT have the same break cost at the compaction event under the post-U13 library. Median break cost: fork 5132.75 uncached tokens, summarise-in-place 442.25; median paired delta +4774.25 (range -2035..+5611.5; 95% bootstrap CI [193.5, 4868.25]; 15/18 pairs positive, sign test p=0.0075). The three negative pairs are all at event index 2, where both arms recorded cached_tokens=0 (an across-the-board full miss, not a policy effect): excluding that stratum, n=15, median +4839.5, CI [4677.5, 4901.5], 15/15 positive, p=6.1e-05.
caveats: The summarise arm's ~4.3k-token reuse depends on the deterministic prefix-truncating summariser: successive summaries are nested prefixes. A real abstractive summariser would not guarantee that, so the magnitude is summariser-dependent; the fork marker's effect (break starts in the header and at the first body byte) is not.

Server-side cache retention is noisy and not instrumented: at every event-2 turn both arms recorded cached_tokens=0, and steady-state cached values alternate between 6144, 6464 and 4352. The paired design absorbs most of it via the neighbouring-turn baseline, but the noise is why the full-18 CI is wide ([193.5, 4868.25]).

The fork arm's prompt is larger by the marker+label: server prompt_tokens delta at events has median 411 and range 189-621 (growing with each fold because summaries nest earlier markers). That is a property of the post-U13 encoding, not a measurement error.
This run answers the *event* question only; it says nothing about total uncached cost over the whole conversation (that is U15's question) and no steady-state winner is claimed.

evidence.deviation_and_remainder: Design target was 3 sessions x 44 turns / 7 events / 21 pairs, which needs 264 live requests (3x44x2; 258 trimming to the last neighbour) -- over the hard 200 cap. Ran the largest symmetric design that fits: 38 turns, 6 events, 18 pairs, 195 requests (11 shared pre-fork requests + 2x27). Remainder: event 7 (turn 42) and its 3 pairs. It cannot be topped up by appending turns 39-43, because the pre-event cache state would be cold; getting it needs a 44-turn rerun at a raised cap.

green.claim: post-U13 arms differ at/after the fork point, identical before it

red.claim: with the fork marker removed (pre-U13 library, unlabelled POINTER) the two arms are byte-identical at every turn and the analysis refuses
red.guard_error: 162 distinctness failure(s); first: u4-s1 turn 12: arms render byte-identical prompts at/after the event -- the U4 defect

evidence.mechanism: Within-arm contrast at events 3-6: the fork arm's event-turn cached_tokens is 64 against 6464-6528 on its neighbouring turns (it re-prefills essentially the whole prompt), while the summarise arm's event-turn cached_tokens is 4352/4416, the same as its own neighbours. Two causes, both intrinsic to the post-U13 encoding: (a) the content-addressed fork root is labelled in the invariant header and that label changes at every fold, so the break starts inside message 0 (observed first-diff byte offset 222 is in the header; cached falls to the pre-label 64-token block); (b) the fork root body begins with the unique [fork] marker (offset 302), so nothing after the header can prefix-match.

excluding_event_index_2.why: at event 2 both arms recorded cached_tokens=0 (an across-the-board full miss, not a policy effect); reported, not dropped silently

evidence.pre_fork_sharing: Turns 1-11 are byte-identical across arms (no fork exists yet), so one request serves both and is written as one row per arm with shared_request=true (66 rows from 33 requests). The identical-prompt fact is asserted in the live loop before every shared send and re-checked by the analysis guard.
